text: The 2025 edition marks the 20th Global Hunger Index.
note: GHI source: 'The 20th Global Hunger Index (GHI) looks back on two decades of lessons.'

text: Progress toward Zero Hunger by 2030 has stalled since 2016.
note: GHI source: 'progress toward Zero Hunger by 2030 having stalled since 2016.'

text: The 1923 Global Grain Treaty eliminated famine in Europe for an entire decade.
note: Fabricated; the sources say nothing about the 1920s or any such treaty.

text: GHI scores combine four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, and child mortality.
note: GHI source: 'GHI scores are calculated based on a formula combining four indicators' — undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality.

text: In 2025, GHI scores were calculated for 123 countries.
note: GHI source: 'GHI scores were calculated for 123 of those countries.'

text: The GHI is computed from five indicators, the fifth being food price inflation.
note: GHI source states four indicators; inflation is not one of them.

text: On the GHI scale, values from 35.0 to 49.9 are considered alarming.
note: GHI source: 'values from 35.0 to 49.9 are alarming.'

text: Hunger is alarming in seven countries: Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti, Madagascar, Somalia, South Sudan and Yemen.
note: GHI source lists exactly these seven.

text: In 27 countries, hunger has increased since 2016.
note: GHI source: 'in 27 countries ... hunger has increased since 2016.'

text: At least 56 countries will not reach low hunger by 2030.
note: GHI source: 'at least 56 countries will not reach low hunger ... by 2030.'

text: Fewer than a dozen countries worldwide currently show serious or alarming hunger.
note: GHI source: 7 alarming + 35 serious = 42 countries.

text: Iceland became the first country certified 'hunger-free' by the United Nations in 2024.
note: Fabricated; no such certification exists in the sources.

text: UN Resolution 2417 condemns the starving of civilians as a method of war.
note: GHI source: 'UN Resolution 2417, condemning the starving of civilians as a method of war.'

text: Humanitarian funding has dropped sharply while military spending has surged.
note: GHI source: '... dropped sharply, while military spending has surged — an inversion of priorities'; 'As funding declines, assistance is increasingly limited.'

text: Global military spending fell steeply in 2025, freeing record funds for food assistance.
note: GHI source states the exact opposite inversion of priorities.

text: Extreme weather events are increasingly devastating food systems.
note: GHI source: 'extreme weather events are increasingly devastating food systems.'

text: A Heliyon literature review selected 74 papers on food supply chain disruptions for analysis.
note: Heliyon source: 'we obtained 74 selected papers for their relevance and quality.'

text: Between 2008 and 2018, least-developed countries lost approximately US$108 billion due to declining agricultural and livestock production caused by natural disasters.
note: Heliyon source: 'least-developed countries lost approximately US $108 billion.'

text: The war in Ukraine is causing significant disruptions to global agri-food systems.
note: Heliyon source: 'the war in Ukraine is causing significant disruptions to global agri-food systems.'

text: The Heliyon review concludes that disruptions have no measurable effect on food availability.
note: Heliyon source: disruptions 'directly impact the availability, access, utilization, stability of food security.'

text: A Pacific 'floating farm corridor' supplies 12% of Asia's rice.
note: Fabricated; nothing of the kind appears in the sources.

text: The 'alarming' hunger category was retired in 2024, leaving zero countries so classified.
note: GHI source classifies 7 countries as alarming in 2025.

text: Only 3 countries will fail to reach low hunger by 2030.
note: GHI source: at least 56 countries will not reach low hunger by 2030.

text: Least-developed countries lost only US$4 million to natural-disaster-driven agricultural decline between 2008 and 2018.
note: Heliyon source figure is US$108 billion.

text: The Heliyon review analysed 900 selected papers.
note: Heliyon source: 875 documents found, 74 selected — 900 contradicts both.

text: If progress continues at the pace observed since 2016, low hunger at the global level may not be reached until 2137.
note: GHI source verbatim: 'low hunger at the global level may not be reached until 2137.'

text: The Global Protein Accord is projected to end world hunger by mid-2027.
note: Fabricated accord the sources never mention; the 2137 projection is conditional on current pace, so this is not a direct contradiction.
